title: FNAF OC Base: Start an Original Design Responsibly (Unofficial)
summary: How to start an unofficial FNAF-inspired OC from a blank base without tracing official art. Fan content only.
body_markdown:
> **Unofficial fan content.** This page is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or associated with Scott Cawthon, Steel Wool Studios, or any official Five Nights at Freddy's rights holders. Five Nights at Freddy's and related names are trademarks of their owners. We discuss **original characters** inspired by the vibe of horror-animatronic stories—never official assets, and we make no trademark claims.


> **Quick answer:** A “base” is a blank body or mannequin you customize. Use original or clearly permissively licensed bases. Do not trace official artwork or claim a base is endorsed.


Hub:[fnaf-oc-maker](https://www.redbean.ai/blog/fnaf-oc-maker)


Table of Contents


Toggle


##


What people mean by OC base


#


- Blank doll / mannequin for dress-up
- Simple front-view template for markers or digital layers
- Picrew-style part makers (general, not brand-affiliated)


##


Responsible checklist


#


- Read the base creator's rules.
- Credit when required.
- Change enough that the character is yours.
- Never upload official game assets as a "base."
- Label posts unofficial fan OC.


##


A clean starter process


#


- Pick proportions (tall lanky tech vs compact performer).
- Block silhouette in one color.
- Add one signature feature.
- Outfit and prop.
- Fill the[template](https://www.redbean.ai/blog/fnaf-oc-template) .


##


Digital vs paper


#


Paper is great for silhouette drills. Digital layers help with variants (day mode / night mode). Either way, personality notes matter more than polish for roleplay.


##


Layer order suggestion (digital)


#


- Body base
- Head / faceplate
- Outfit
- Prop
- Effects (glow, cracks) sparingly
- Notes layer for arrows and reminders


##


Printable practice


#


Draw five silhouettes in two minutes each. Pick the clearest. Detail only that one. Speed builds better OCs than perfectionism.


##


Keep notes outside the app


#


Whatever tool you try, keep a short external note with the character or pet name, the goal for this week, and three facts that must not drift. Apps change. Your notes travel.

##


Red flags on random "bases" from the internet


#


- Watermarks from official art
- No license text
- Requests to remove credit against the artist's wishes
- Bundles that include trademarked logos


Walk away from those.
